data.scenario_text: A zipline runs in a straight line from the top of a launch platform to an anchor point on the ground. The zipline is <m>160</m> feet long, and the angle of depression from the top of the platform to the anchor point is <m>28^\circ</m>.
data.find_task: Find the horizontal distance from the base of the platform to the anchor point. Do not round until the final answer; then round to two decimal places as necessary.
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). A correct sketch shows a right triangle with the right angle marked, the given 28^\circ angle placed at the correct vertex, and the one given length written on its correct side: the hypotenuse is 160\text{ ft}. The other two side lengths are not given, so they stay unlabeled. The 28^\circ angle belongs at the anchor point on the ground, not at the top of the platform: the angle of depression stated at the top and the angle of elevation at the anchor are alternate interior angles, with the horizontal through the top of the platform parallel to the ground.

Part (b). The angle of depression is measured downward from a horizontal line through the top of the platform. That line is parallel to the ground, so the angle of depression and the angle of elevation from the anchor point are alternate interior angles and are therefore congruent. The 28^\circ angle sits inside the triangle at the anchor point.

Read the triangle from that angle: the horizontal distance from the base of the platform to the anchor point is the leg adjacent to the given angle, and the known quantity is the hypotenuse. The one basic ratio that uses exactly those two sides is cosine, \cos\theta=\dfrac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}, so that is the ratio to use.

Substituting and computing, d=160\cos(28^\circ).

So the horizontal distance from the base of the platform to the anchor point is \boxed{141.27\text{ ft}}.
